chunks.text: Ukraine {{carried out}} a large drone offensive that lasted about three days. Ukraine said its forces {{stepped up}} attacks on Russian [[oil tankers]] and [[refineries]]. One Ukrainian commander described the campaign as reaching an "industrial scale." According to reports, the [[drones]] {{set off}} fires at several energy sites, and Ukraine claimed it had hit 21 [[vessels]], including 19 oil tankers, near Crimea.

chunks.text: Scientists have {{found out}} that giraffes can do simple math. Researchers at the University of Barcelona {{carried out}} a study with four giraffes at a zoo in Spain. They wanted to see whether the animals could {{work out}} which [[amount]] of food was bigger. The results surprised many people.

chunks.text: China has {{pulled off}} a major step in [[space travel]]. From the Hainan Commercial Space Launch Site, a new rocket called the Long March-10B {{took off}}, carried a [[satellite]] into [[orbit]], and then guided its huge lower part, or [[booster]], safely back to Earth. China became only the second country, after the United States, to recover an orbital rocket so it can be used again.

chunks.text: The European Union has {{spoken out}} against two of the world's most popular apps. Officials said that Instagram and Facebook, which are both owned by the company Meta, are designed to be too [[addictive]]. They believe the apps break a European law called the Digital Services Act, because their design can harm users' health and [[wellbeing]].

chunks.text: The [[regulators]] {{pointed out}} three features that keep people using the apps for hours. One feature, called [[infinite scroll]], lets a [[feed]] load forever; videos {{start up}} on their own through [[autoplay]]; and the app keeps {{serving up}} posts it thinks you will like. Together, officials said, these tricks push the brain into "autopilot," so users {{end up}} scrolling without really deciding to.
